#5301. Binance’s $6.3B Hack Fix Is Coming Tomorrow: Why the ZK Math Doesn't Tell the Whole Story

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

At the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot shows its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

Blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham says those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

If Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

The FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

It shows how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own users. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

While the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now shows:

The first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what users hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:

Why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:

The striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, showed BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:

Not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

How Binance says it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

What the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It shows the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance says the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest update says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:

The design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

What it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

What customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

Immediate support sits at 76,000–76,500, right where the long-term moving average meets the price. If sellers push through, the next downside targets are around $74,000 and $72,000. A deeper correction could eventually bring the $70,000 psychological level into play.

To stabilize at all, Bitcoin first needs to reclaim $78,000. Even then, heavier resistance is waiting between $80,000 and $82,000, where several moving averages bunch together.

The daily RSI has slipped to the mid-30s. Sellers are gaining momentum, and while the indicator is getting close to oversold, it hasn't given a convincing reversal signal yet. Selling volume was high during the decline as well, so sellers are still very much active.

Bitcoin's next move depends largely on one question: can buyers defend the 200-day moving average?

If it rebounds above $78,000, a recovery toward 80,000–82,000 could follow. A confirmed break below $76,000, on the other hand, would strengthen the bearish case and make a longer correction toward $72,000 more likely.

Bitcoin is at an inflection point. For now, sellers have the short-term advantage.

XRP lost a key support region near $1.30, and the bearish pressure is growing. As of October 30 it was trading around $1.2352, extending its recent decline after repeatedly failing to hold momentum above $1.40.

The daily XRP/USD chart shows lower highs, weakening momentum and a break below several moving averages. After September's rally toward $1.60, XRP started to correct, and the recovery attempts since then never turned into a lasting uptrend. That left it open to more selling.

Now the latest drop has pushed XRP below its major moving averages, the 200-day near 1.36–1.37 included, which keeps the bearish picture intact.

The nearest support is around $1.20–$1.22. The latest intraday lows are there, and $1.20 is a round number besides.

If XRP breaks below $1.20 and the break is confirmed, selling pressure could speed up toward $1.15 and then the $1.10 support area. If sellers keep control, the $1.00 psychological level could become a longer-term target.

On the upside, the first resistance is between $1.28 and $1.30. Reclaiming it would be an early sign that selling is easing. Above that, 1.33–1.37 is tougher, since several moving averages meet there.

RSI has fallen to the low 30s, which signals strong bearish momentum and puts XRP close to oversold. Oversold readings can lead to short rebounds. They don't prove the bottom is in, though.

Volume was also higher on the way down, giving the breakdown more weight.

Short term, XRP stays bearish while it trades below $1.30. A recovery above that level could let buyers try for the 1.35–1.40 resistance zone, but as long as XRP is under the major moving averages, sellers keep the upper hand.

And if the $1.20 region fails, the correction could stretch toward $1.15 and possibly $1.10. Until buyers reclaim the key resistance levels, the downside risks remain high.

Ethereum (ETH) has extended its slide, dropping below $2,300 as sellers took more control. On the daily chart, ETH trades near $2,222.59 after a sharp rejection from the 2,350–2,400 resistance region.

It's been a big drop from the October peak near $2,800. The series of lower highs and lower lows points to a bearish trend, and that comes after a strong recovery in August and September.

The latest sell-off took ETH below every major moving average on the chart. The most worrying part is the break below the longer-term averages around 2,300–2,360, which used to act as support.

Buyers may try to hold the nearest support at 2,170–2,200. A clear break below it could speed the selling up toward $2,100 and then the $2,000 threshold.

To ease the downside pressure, Ethereum needs to win back $2,300. There's more resistance near $2,350, and a sustained move above $2,450 would be a more convincing sign that buyers are returning.

RSI sits near the lower edge of its neutral range, in line with steady selling. ETH is getting close to oversold, but the indicator hasn't confirmed a bullish reversal.

Heavy trading volume during the decline only adds to the worries about sentiment. The wider crypto sell-off also came at the same time as reports of a major Binance security incident, which added uncertainty across digital assets.

#5298. BNB Crypto Drops 8.7% in an Hour as Binance Loses $6.36 Billion to Hackers, and Futures Traders Turn Short: Can BNB Hold Its 200-Day Average?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour after the Binance hack and is lagging Bitcoin, as shorts pile in. Can BNB hold its 200-day EMA at $692?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour on Thursday, October 29, from $744.90 to $680, as hackers drained about $6.36 billion from Binance, the exchange behind the token, in the largest crypto theft on record. The bounce since has been the weakest among the big coins. BNB trades at $702, down 6.2% in 24 hours, with a $92.4 billion market cap and 48.7% below its $1,370 record from October 2025. In futures, traders who bet against it are now paying to keep those bets open.

So why is BNB taking the hack harder than Bitcoin, what happened to it after Binance’s last two security scares, and where are the levels that matter?

If a $6.3B security breach can't completely break $BNB, what will?

The market is testing @BNBCHAIN resilience right now.

Historically, moments of maximum fear can create the best opportunities.

Because it is the coin most tied to Binance itself, and futures traders are now betting on that link. From the 20:00 UTC price on Thursday, BNB is still down 5.6%, more than Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP or Dogecoin.

Large-cap coins since the Binance hack. Source: Binance

The hack itself didn’t touch BNB Chain. TRM Labs’ breakdown lists ten blockchains the attacker drained Binance wallets on, from Ethereum to Polygon, and BNB Chain isn’t among them. What traders are pricing is the exchange: BNB is Binance’s token, so a hit to Binance reads as a hit to BNB.

“The Binance exploit has intensified market-wide selling, with BNB facing the greatest exposure,” Zeus Research analyst Dominick John said. Rick Maeda of Laevitas saw it the other way, calling the drop “quite modest for possibly the largest exchange theft ever.”

The futures market sides with the bears. On OKX:

Put together, that reads as many small accounts buying the dip and fewer, larger traders shorting it. If BNB bounces, those shorts are fuel for a squeeze. If it breaks lower, the crowded longs are.

It fell further at first, then recovered within a month both times. Binance has been here twice before:

This time BNB is 8.7% under its pre-hack price at its worst so far. If it follows either path, there could be another leg down before any recovery.

The comparison traders keep reaching for is FTT, the FTX token that lost almost all its value when the exchange collapsed in November 2022. The difference is the balance sheet. FTX had spent customer money and couldn’t pay it back. Binance says it will cover all losses from this hack, and Tether, Circle and others froze about $2.7 billion of the stolen funds within hours.

Traders haven’t fully relaxed, though. Binance hasn’t said how it will fund the payout, and withdrawals stay shut until the reopening it expects within 48 hours of its Friday morning update.

It is holding by a thin margin. BNB closed Thursday at $698.46, just above its 200-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $692.46, after the hack-hour wick to $680 dipped below it. The 50-day EMA at $733.06 is now overhead.

The four-month chart puts BNB back where it was in late August. It traded between $674.60 and $726 for two weeks before breaking out in early September and running to $809.99 on October 5. Thursday’s drop erased that whole move.

For BNB crypto, the next 48 hours carry more weight than any chart line. A smooth reopening of Binance withdrawals would leave the shorts on the wrong side of a crowded trade. A delay, or any sign Binance is selling BNB to pay for the hack, would put $674.60 in play.

#5296. Why November's +80% History Is a Statistical Flaw for XRP Holders

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. XRP's 15.7% drop in October has brought the token to the most unpredictable crossroads of the year. Historical data from thirteen years of observations promise the market harsh November volatility. However, behind the optimistic figures of past years lies a serious methodological flaw capable of disorienting investors amid the current pressure.

The main trap for the market is the asymmetry of returns. According to Cryptorank, XRP's average November gain is an impressive +80.2%, but this figure is completely distorted by two isolated anomalies: a surge of +531.9% in 2013 and a rally of +281.7% in 2024. The month's median, a negative -10%, reflects reality much more accurately.

Historically, in most cycles, XRP closed November in the red. The fourth quarter, which so far consists of October alone, is already down -16.3%, in line with the asset's seasonal tendency toward correction that the averaged statistics mask.

The median is not a perfect guide either: thirteen observations are a small sample, and the market structure has changed. Since spot XRP ETFs launched in the US in mid-November 2025, the token has had an institutional demand channel that did not exist in earlier cycles.

Mathematical pessimism is reinforced by the real balance of power on the market at the end of October. The XRP price has fallen below the key support line of $1.30 and is trading around $1.25–$1.26, marking a local downtrend.

All the upward momentum built on investors' expectations has faded, opening the way for profit-taking by short-term players. Notably, the October decline follows a 48% gain in the third quarter, XRP's best Q3 in four years, which suggests that at least part of the current pressure is profit-taking after the rally rather than seasonality alone.

The situation is aggravated by an inevitable influx of supply amid a liquidity shortage. On Sunday, November 1, a scheduled unlock of 1 billion XRP from Ripple's escrow wallets will take place.

It is worth noting, however, that the escrow unlock is a routine monthly event that has followed the same schedule since 2017, and Ripple typically returns 600–800 million XRP to new escrow contracts. The real net addition to circulating supply is therefore closer to 200–400 million XRP.

Even so, against the backdrop of thin liquidity, this volume is enough to put additional pressure on the price, as it will enter the market simultaneously with macroeconomic pressure and the aftermath of the recent wave of forced liquidations of long positions worth more than $1.29 billion, caused by a security incident at the Binance exchange.

At the same time, the wave of liquidations has partially cleared excess leverage from the market. If funding rates stay negative and open interest does not recover, the bearish scenario may be capped by a short squeeze, which would make a retest of $1.30–$1.32 more likely than the statistics suggest.

The chart, cleared of historical anomalies, points to two scenarios:

#5295. Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying, as Route 2 FI Buys the Dip

Bitcoin news: the Binance hacker holds $1.4B in BTC, 3x this week’s ETF inflows. Will Binance’s buyback help, and can BTC hold $76,500?

Bitcoin news on Friday turned to a warning from trader Route 2 FI, who said the Binance hacker’s $1.4 billion in BTC is more than three times what spot ETFs bought all week, a potential seller hanging over Bitcoin at $77,300.

Arkham’s entity page shows the Binance hacker holding 18,270 BTC worth $1.42 billion and 488,364 ETH worth $1.09 billion across 73 addresses. US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million from Monday to Thursday.

Route 2 FI still likes the setup enough to take a position. The trader expects Binance to recover fully but thinks the hack will push more people toward decentralized exchanges.

Binance would need a couple of months to fill this hole, unless they use other shady tactics to get whole faster.

The hacker has $BTC worth $1.4b and $ETH worth $1b ready to sell. For $BTC, that's more than 3x the $450M that spot ETFs bought all week.

— Route 2 FI (@Route2FI) October 30, 2026

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Holds $79,200 Before the Fed, Coinbase Earnings and a $10.9B Expiry: Which Way Next?

Route 2 FI’s math holds up. Arkham’s Binance Hacker entity shows 18,270 BTC, worth $1.42 billion at Friday’s prices. SoSoValue figures show US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million across four straight days of inflows from October 26 to 29. That makes the hacker’s Bitcoin about 3.2 times a week of ETF demand.

Binance hacker holdings on October 30, 2026 vs spot Bitcoin ETF inflows for October 26 to 29. Sources: Arkham, SoSoValue.

The hacker hasn’t sold any of the Bitcoin yet. The selling so far has been in smaller tokens: Lookonchain tracked the attacker dumping UNI, PEPE, ENA, LINK and others for 70,480 ETH, worth about $158 million.

On the other side, Binance is already buying. The exchange told CoinDesk it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover the losses, $5 billion of it already held in the same tokens the attackers took, and is buying the rest on exchanges and over the counter. About $3 billion of the stolen funds is frozen and doesn’t need replacing.

“Binance’s SAFU fund and Binance’s holdings include a large amount of assets such as BTC and ETH. We are currently buying, through OTC and on-exchange, all the stolen altcoins in fully matching amounts.”

That matters for Bitcoin. If Binance already holds enough BTC to cover customers, its buying lands mostly on altcoins, which leaves the hacker’s 18,270 BTC as a seller without a matching buyer.

Route 2 FI pointed to the Bybit hack as the template. Attackers took about $1.4 billion in ether from Bybit on February 21, 2025, and the exchange replaced it within days through loans, deposits and market purchases.

The buyback gave prices only a short lift. Measured from the February 20, 2025 close on Binance:

Ethereum bounced while Bybit bought, then lost more than a third of its value within three weeks. The broader market sold off over that stretch for reasons beyond the hack, so the table shows that buyback demand fades fast. It doesn’t show that the hack caused the slide.

Route 2 FI also argued that the hack, coming a year after the October 10, 2025 crash, gives traders another reason to keep less money on centralized exchanges. Binance paid out more than $283 million in compensation after that crash, when some assets lost their pegs on its platform.

The trader cited the jump in Hyperliquid’s HYPE token as proof. The timing doesn’t fit, though. HYPE rose from $79.38 to a $97.09 high between 10:00 and 16:00 UTC on Thursday, after ICE and Trade.xyz announced plans for a regulated US perpetuals venue on Hyperliquid. That was about ten hours before the Binance drain began at 20:04 UTC.

After the hack, HYPE fell to $88.55 and trades at $90.83.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Whale Sends $35M to Coinbase at a $15M Loss as October Turns Red: What Moves BTC Next?

The setup Route 2 FI is buying is easy to see on the daily chart since early August. Bitcoin’s $76,500 low on Friday stopped $35 above its 200-day EMA at $76,465, a line it has closed above every day since the late-August breakout. BTC trades at $77,326, down 3.5% in 24 hours.

August 2 to October 30, 2026: BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

The last time Bitcoin tested the 200-day line, in mid-September, it held at $74,968 and climbed to $87,395 within a week. A trader buying here has a clear line to be wrong at.

For Bitcoin news over the coming week, two things decide which row plays out: whether Binance reopens withdrawals on schedule, and whether the hacker’s Bitcoin starts to move.

#5294. XRP Reserves on Binance Hit Lowest Level Since 2022

As the broader crypto market continues to face intense selling pressure due to the prolonged market volatility seen over the past weeks, XRP appears to be seeing rising demand instead.

While its price is also struggling amid the market downturn, onchain data from crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant shows that more tokens are leaving major exchanges instead, which could be interpreted as intense buying.

The data shows that XRP reserves on the world's largest exchange by volume, Binance, have dropped to their lowest level since December 2022.

As of October 30, Binance has seen its XRP reserve fall to 2.47 billion XRP from the 2.69 billion XRP it recorded on October 28, marking a sharp decline in its holdings in just two days.

This signals rapid accumulation from traders as it marks a decrease of about 8.18% in the amount of XRP available for sale on Binance, with over  220 million XRP withdrawn in just a two-day period.

While decreases in exchange reserves simply mean a reduction in the amount of XRP readily available for trading, it potentially reduces immediate selling pressure if demand remains steady, thereby providing a bullish outlook for the token.

Further data shows that the decrease in the XRP exchange reserve on Binance has coincided with falling XRP balances on several other major crypto exchanges, including Bybit and Bithumb.

The data shows that reductions seen on these exchanges were smaller compared to Binance, as Bybit's XRP reserves dropped from 306 million to 286 million XRP during the same period.

Bithumb, on the other hand, also recorded a decrease of 10 million XRP, with its reserves falling from 1.847 billion to 1.837 billion XRP, down approximately 0.54% during the same days.

While this indicates a broader reduction in exchange-held supply and XRP has remained volatile despite the shrinking supply, it is important to note that lower balances do not always mean that investors are accumulating XRP, which could be the reason XRP has yet to react to the trend.

#5293. 'XRP at 100'? Ripple CTO Emeritus Reveals Surprising Story Behind Iconic T-Shirt

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz has revealed the unexpected story behind an iconic XRP-themed T-shirt he wore at the Swell event, explaining how a technical milestone on the XRP Ledger became associated with a memorable price moment.

Schwartz, one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger (XRPL), was spotted wearing a T-shirt that showed a 'speedometer'-like inscription that pointed to 100, sparking curiosity among members of the XRP community.

X user @unknowDLT had asked Schwartz about the origin of the T-shirt he wore in an image that accompanied his tweet. "At this point, could you clearly explain what the T-shirt you're wearing means?" he asked.

@unknowDLT It was created to commemorate XRPL hitting 100 TPS. When we commissioned it, XRP was around 30 cents. By the time we got it, XRP was $1. So everyone thought that's what XRP at 100 meant and we just went with it.

Schwartz responded that the T-shirt was created to commemorate XRPL hitting 100 TPS. "When the T-shirt was commissioned, XRP was around 30 cents. By the time we got it, XRP was $1," Schwartz further explained.

The timing caused some members of the XRP community to assume the "100" on the shirt referred to XRP reaching a price of $1 rather than the network's transaction speed.

"So everyone thought that's what XRP at 100 meant and we just went with it," Schwartz added.

In the X discussion, the Ripple CTO Emeritus did not share exact details on the time when the T-shirt was commissioned.

XRP also traded around 30 cents ($0.30) at several points in its price history, so it may be hard to know exactly when, in the context of the Ripple CTO Emeritus's post. A walk-through of the XRP Ledger throughput chronology may provide a hint.

When performance testing began in February 2015, the XRP Ledger sustained 80 transactions per second. Incremental improvements were made over time as opportunities were uncovered.

Between March and June 2015, the XRP Ledger sustained between 120 and 490 transactions per second. In October 2015, XRPL saw a major throughput boost to 525 transactions per second, and in the following year, this nearly doubled to 1,100 transactions per second.

In July 2017, XRP was demonstrated to sustain a throughput of 1,500 transactions per second, which remains so to this day.

A Mexico City lawmaker has proposed tough new penalties for people who steal electricity to mine cryptocurrency. Alberto Martínez Urincho wants to amend Mexico’s Federal Criminal Code so that illegal power use for mining carries a prison term of 5 to 12 years, Publimetro reported. Offenders would also face fines of 1,000 to 3,000 UMA units, Mexico’s official benchmark for setting fines, and lose their equipment. Sentences could rise to 18 years in more serious cases, such as tapping into high-voltage lines, causing major disruption to power supply or running hidden data centres. The plan targets unauthorised power connections, not legal crypto mining. It still needs approval from the Mexico City legislature and must pass through the federal lawmaking process.

The Dogecoin community gets a security alert after wallet provider Trezor revealed a suspected hardware implant in its Safe 5 device bought from CryptoBilis.

Dogecoin community member Mishaboar urged users who purchased a Trezor device from CryptoBilis in March this year or later to take immediate precautions, including moving their funds to a completely new wallet with a freshly generated recovery seed.

"If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis in March 2026 or later, move your funds to a completely new wallet, with a newly generated recovery seed, as soon as possible," Mishaboar wrote.

If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis in March 2026 or later, move your funds to a completely new wallet, with a newly generated recovery seed, as soon as possible. Use a device and wallet you trust to create the new wallet. If your wallet supports an additional passphrase, use it (and remember to write it down in your offline backups). NEVER reuse a recovery seed from a wallet that might have been compromised. Simply resetting the device or importing the same seed into another wallet does NOT make your funds safe. An ELI5: I know this is obvious to many of you, but in my experience some people don't realize that hardware wallets don't actually "contain" their coins. Your coins "live" on the blockchain. Your wallet only holds the keys that allow you to access and spend them. If someone else has a copy of those keys, they can access your funds from anywhere in the world, from any device where those keys are imported. They don't need your physical little device or your phone to access it.

Users are warned never to reuse a recovery seed from a wallet that might have been compromised. Simply resetting the device or importing the same seed into another wallet does not make funds safe either.

Mishaboar highlighted a critical security principle that may not seem obvious to all users: hardware wallets do not actually "contain" coins—the coins "live" on the blockchain. The wallet only holds the keys that allow access to and spending of the coins. If someone obtains these keys, they can access the funds from anywhere in the world on any device where the keys are imported, without needing the physical device or the user's phone.

Mishaboar's warning follows a recent update from Trezor regarding CryptoBilis, in which the company disclosed that it had been alerted through responsible disclosure to a suspected hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device purchased from CryptoBilis in August 2026.

According to Trezor, the reported device has not yet been received for physical examination. However, the company said it considers the report credible enough to notify customers while its security team investigates. No CryptoBilis buyer has reported losing funds to the company so far.

In light of this, affected users are urged to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible. Those who have not yet set up their device should never do so using an existing wallet backup (recovery phrase), nor share this information with anyone.

It's the 18th anniversary of the Bitcoin whitepaper. Today marks the historic date on which its pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto published the blueprint for the first digital cash.

On Oct. 31, 2008, a nine-page white paper called "Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System" was published, laying out a radical vision for transferring value electronically without the need for conventional financial intermediaries.

Bitcoin supporters, exchanges, and the rest of the crypto community are filling social media platform X with celebratory wishes on the 18th anniversary of Bitcoin's unveiling to the world.

Bitcoin proponent and Strategy Chairman Michael Saylor wrote on X: "Happy Bitcoin white paper day. 18 years."

One of the most salient features of the whitepaper is the fixed supply of Bitcoin at 21 million coins. The pre-determined issuance structure is what makes Bitcoin different from traditional monetary systems, where central authorities can inflate the money supply.

Major U.S. crypto exchange Coinbase highlighted this fact in its X post: "21,000,000. Never more. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day."

21,000,000. Never more. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day. https://t.co/JtKeHtCuSM

"Today marks 18 years since the release of the Bitcoin Whitepaper. A day that changed everything," Coinbase continued.

Stablecoin issuer Tether wrote: "On 31 October 2008, Satoshi published nine pages that explained Bitcoin to the world. Today we're explaining it to everyone else. Two pizzas, 10,000 BTC, 21 million coins, and one key you never share. Everything you need to know, in a comic. Happy 18th birthday, Bitcoin whitepaper."

Crypto platform Uphold wrote: "Nine pages that challenged the entire legacy financial system. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day."

The Bitcoin whitepaper laid the groundwork for the network's launch in January 2009, when Satoshi Nakamoto mined Bitcoin's genesis block and introduced the first units of the cryptocurrency.

When Bitcoin launched on January 3, 2009, it had no market value or official exchange price. Over the years, Bitcoin has evolved from a niche technological experiment into a globally recognized digital asset. Its emergence has influenced the development of thousands of cryptocurrencies, blockchain applications, and decentralized financial systems.

The cryptocurrency now trades at $77,310 and is worth $1.55 trillion, according to CoinMarketCap data.

#5283. BTCPay Server Tells Merchants to Shut Down After Attackers Sweep Hot Wallets: Are Payments Still Safe?

Bitcoin news: BTCPay Server told merchants to go offline after attackers swept hot wallets on 2.4.1 or older. Here is who is exposed.

In today’s Bitcoin news, BTCPay Server, the free open-source payment processor many Bitcoin merchants run themselves, told every operator to shut down their instance after reports that attackers were sweeping the hot wallets on merchant servers. Less than six hours later, the culprit was old software.

At 04:07 UTC on Monday, the project said its investigation had found an attack vector aimed at servers running version 2.4.1, released on July 23, or older. It has “no credible reports” of drains on the current 2.4.7. BTCPay has not said how much was stolen or how many stores were hit.

That makes this a different kind of Bitcoin news from last week’s Binance hack. No exchange was breached. Merchants who run their own payment stack, the people self-custody is meant to protect, were the target.

So who was exposed, and what should store owners do now?

Unauthorized attackers are reportedly draining hot wallets on @BtcpayServer instances.

Users running BTCPay Server instances are advised to shut them down immediately. pic.twitter.com/H7mXfJLLcD

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 2, 2026

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

An attacker logged in as admin on older servers and emptied the hot wallets. BTCPay Server raised the alarm at 22:25 UTC on Sunday and asked operators to run its shutdown script “until we complete the investigation.”

Two hours later, founder Nicolas Dorier said the project’s own public servers on 2.4.7 were not attacked. “The attacker managed to log in as admin on those instance, we are still trying to figure out how,” he wrote.

📢 Our incident response investigation identified an attack vector targeting instances running versions 2.4.1 (Jul 23, 2026) or older.

We have no credible reports of hot wallet drains for users running the latest 2.4.7 release. We again urge everyone to keep their BTCPay Server… pic.twitter.com/gYxK4Bb7fc

— BTCPay Server (@BtcpayServer) November 2, 2026

A hot wallet keeps its signing keys on the server itself, so it can pay out refunds and payouts automatically. Anyone with admin rights on that server can send the coins too.

Hosting providers moved fast. BTCPay thanked LunaNode and others for shutting down older hosted instances on their own, so some merchants may find their store offline on Monday.

The version history is the story. 2.4.1 shipped on July 23. Two weeks later, 2.4.2 fixed a critical flaw the team said was “being actively exploited,” and five more releases followed, ending with Thursday’s 2.4.7, which fixed 85 findings from an AI security scan Anthropic ran for the project.

Whether this is the same hole as August’s is still open. Dorier said a blog post with more detail is coming.

Only if it still runs 2.4.1 or older, on what the project knows so far. “For those who already updated at least once since the release of 2.4.2, there is no reason to panic,” Dorier wrote at 04:10 UTC.

The reported drains all hit hot wallets. Stores that receive into a watch-only wallet keep their signing keys off the server altogether.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

No. BTC sat at $77,890 when the alert went out and traded at $78,102 on Binance at 07:40 UTC on Monday, up 0.3% in a day. The market is still chewing on last week’s Binance hack.

That hack set the floor. Bitcoin fell to $76,326 on October 30, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average), now at $76,512, and buyers have held above it for three days. Above, the 50-day EMA at $80,293 is now overhead, and $81,971, the October 29 high before the hack, caps the range.

The Fear & Greed Index reads 37, fear, and BTC is down 2.5% on the week.

The CSI 300 fell 8.5% in October, marking its worst monthly performance since early 2016.

China's technology-focused STAR 50 index has dropped around 40% from its June peak, wiping out approximately $480 billion in market value.

Fresh government support measures have failed to restore investor confidence, with AI concerns and economic weakness continuing to weigh on equities.

China’s stock market is facing one of its toughest periods in more than a decade as investors retreat from technology shares and reassess the country’s economic outlook. The CSI 300 has extended its losing streak to 12 consecutive weeks, falling 15% over the period and recording an 8.5% monthly decline in October. The latest selling has continued into November, despite Beijing announcing fresh measures to stabilise the market. Here are the three key factors driving the China stock market sell-off.

The global retreat from artificial intelligence stocks has become a major drag on Chinese equities. Investors are increasingly questioning whether the massive spending on AI infrastructure, semiconductors and computing capacity will generate sufficient returns.

🚨 MASSIVE CRASH IN CHINAOver CN¥1.58 TRILLION ($237B) wiped out from China's stock market as the SSE crashes -1.5%. pic.twitter.com/JMKx8lXDEr

China’s technology sector has been particularly vulnerable. The STAR 50 index, which tracks major technology companies listed on Shanghai’s STAR Market, has fallen around 40% from its late-June peak, erasing approximately $480 billion in market value.

The pressure intensified in October as selling spread across semiconductor and communications equipment companies. On October 30, the CSI 5G communications index dropped 6.2%, while optical module maker Eoptolink Technology plunged 14%. The STAR 50 also fell 5.5% during the session.

The weakness reflects growing concerns about AI valuations and the profitability of heavy capital expenditure. Investors are reassessing whether the expected growth in AI demand can justify the valuations built into technology stocks earlier this year.

Beyond the technology sell-off, persistent economic challenges are weighing on investor confidence. Weak domestic consumption and continued stress in the property sector have raised questions about the strength of China’s economic recovery.

The property market remains a significant concern, particularly as developers continue to face financial pressure. Recent reports that state-owned developer Zhuhai Huafa Group was seeking extensions on certain bank loans have added to worries about debt-related risks in the sector.

These concerns are creating an uncertain outlook for businesses and investors. Weak domestic demand can limit corporate revenue growth, while property-sector stress threatens to weigh on broader economic activity.

The CSI 300’s 8.5% October decline reflects the combination of these domestic challenges and the global technology sell-off. The index also lost 15% over 12 weeks, marking its longest losing streak on record.

Chinese authorities have stepped up efforts to stabilise the stock market following October’s sharp losses. However, the latest measures have yet to convince investors that a sustained recovery is underway.

The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) announced another round of swap operations that could provide more than 100 billion yuan in liquidity to financial institutions for stock purchases. It also made its share-buyback relending programme permanent and reduced the related interest rate from 1.25% to 1%.

Meanwhile, regulators encouraged major listed companies and leading technology firms to buy back shares. They also urged newly launched exchange-traded funds to build positions faster and are considering easing margin requirements to improve market liquidity.

The announcements initially supported a rebound, with the Shanghai Composite rising 1.1% on Monday, November 2. However, Chinese stocks reversed course in early trading on Tuesday, November 3, as investors continued selling technology and energy shares. The CSI 300 and Shanghai Composite both fell roughly 1% in early trade.

The outlook for Chinese equities will depend on whether policymakers can restore confidence and address the economic concerns driving the sell-off. Further liquidity support may help limit short-term volatility, but it may not be enough to reverse the broader downturn.

Investors will closely monitor AI companies’ earnings, domestic consumption and developments in the property sector for signs of improvement. A recovery in technology stocks could also help stabilise broader market sentiment.

For now, the CSI 300’s 8.5% October decline and the continued weakness in technology shares underline the challenges facing China’s equity market. Until investors see stronger earnings prospects and a more convincing economic recovery, the market could remain under pressure.

Crypto hacks and exploits have resulted in more than $11.4 billion in reported losses across 2025 and 2026.

Binance suffered a $6.36 billion breach, with attackers moving most funds within approximately 20 minutes across 10 blockchains.

Hackers also disrupted supermarket refrigeration systems across seven European countries.

The cryptocurrency industry has lost more than $11.4 billion to hacks and exploits across 2025 and 2026. The attacks have exposed weaknesses in exchange infrastructure, wallet security, and blockchain networks.

AI-powered attacks are spreading beyond crypto exchanges, with cyber incidents reported across at least 10 countries in the past 48 hours.

Data from DeFiLlama’s Hacks shows that the crypto industry recorded approximately $2.7 billion in losses during 2025. By 3 November 2026, reported losses had more than tripled to $8.776 billion across 328 incidents.

The February 2025 Bybit hack was one of the year’s biggest attacks, with around $1.5 billion in assets stolen.

However, 2026 has been far more costly, largely due to the 29 October Binance breach, which accounts for $6.36 billion in reported losses.

The Binance attack stands out because of how quickly hackers moved the stolen funds. Investigators traced them through around 12,000 wallets across 11 blockchains in less than four days.

That is roughly one new wallet every 25 seconds.

However, the FBI linked the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking unit, which stole more than $6 billion in virtual assets and converted much of the funds into Ether.

Here are some of the largest crypto attacks reported over the past years.

Artificial intelligence is helping hackers carry out attacks in less time and with less effort.

Google researchers found that attackers built and launched an automated tool to steal login details in under six hours. Anthropic also reported AI-assisted attacks in which hackers completed breaches within two to three hours.

AI can help hackers find weak points in computer systems, create harmful software, steal passwords, and attack several targets at once. This means attacks that once needed large teams and days of preparation can now happen much faster with fewer people.

The cybersecurity concerns have also spread beyond digital assets. Hackers have targeted at least 10 countries in the past 48 hours, disrupting services and spreading false emergency alerts.

The UK has asked households to keep enough food and water for three days, while Japan recommends storing supplies for a full week.

At least 16 countries have issued similar advice.

XRP's burn rate is shooting up toward the end of October, surging 147%. According to data from XRPScan, XRP burned as fees came in at 1,644 on October 30.

The burn activity is a representation of the XRP Ledger's deflationary mechanism, which permanently removes small amounts of XRP from circulation every time transactions are processed on the network.

Some blockchains have scheduled mechanisms to distribute burned tokens, but XRP burns are automatic through transaction fees. Every transaction on the XRP Ledger requires a fee denominated in XRP and that fee is burned.

A total of 14,423,678 XRP, representing 0.014% of its total supply, has been burned so far.

Often referred to as "Uptober" in crypto circles thanks to a track record of outperformance, October might need to shed that nickname given that major cryptocurrencies, including XRP, are down for the month. With few hours left in the month, XRP is down 15.86% so far, on track for its first red month since July.

XRP closed August and September up 30.11% and 7.91% respectively, with traders expecting the positive price run to continue, but this was not to be, as concerns within and outside the market weighed on crypto markets.

The most recent is the Binance heist, which saw $6.3 billion in client assets stolen. In a positive update, Binance said it has covered about 90% of the value of cryptocurrency that hackers stole earlier this week and plans to restore withdrawals by Sunday, making progress on a pledge to fully reimburse customers.

XRP had a nice Q3 2026 and the official XRP X account shared key highlights. The amount of stablecoins on the XRP Ledger increased by 25.2% to $1.03 billion, while net inflows of XRP ETP globally jumped by 39.6% to $355.3 million. Payment volume rose 4.3% to 42.82 billion XRP, while native DEX volume rose 20.2% to $614.8 million. Distributed tokenized RWA value jumped 29.2% to $498.7 million as Aviva's investors launched a tokenized fund with BNY Mellon.

#5276. Binance to Resume XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum and Other Crypto Withdrawals

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance will allow withdrawals for major cryptocurrencies such as XRP, Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL), among others, after suspending withdrawals because of a massive security breach involving $6.3 billion.

Binance announced on Nov. 1 that the exchange would begin resuming withdrawal services between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC.

Binance emphasized that the withdrawal resumption process will be carried out progressively as the exchange conducts security and infrastructure readiness checks.

"We aim to restore withdrawals progressively as we complete security and readiness checks," said Binance.

Binance continued to offer deposit services during the security breach.

The first phase of withdrawal resumption will include a total of 15 blockchain networks.

This list includes popular networks such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Ledger, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, Tron, and Dogecoin.

Other cryptocurrencies that will be available for withdrawals include Zcash (ZEC), Avalanche (AVAX), Sui (SUI), Polygon (POL) and Arbitrum (ARB).

Withdrawals of major stablecoins such as Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) will also be enabled on multiple networks.

The exchange noted that it selected the assets based on user withdrawal demand over the past week.

The exchange also warned that not all listed cryptocurrencies and networks may be enabled at the same time.

The withdrawal resumption comes only days after Binance suffered a massive security breach.

The breach led to the theft of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies from the exchange's hot wallets.

The exchange temporarily paused withdrawals in order to contain the damage, conduct an investigation into the security breach and avoid additional losses.

Binance has now disclosed that it has recovered around 95% of affected assets.

This is up from 90% when Binance last provided an update on the recovery process.

The exchange said that it has fully backed the balances of cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, BNB, USDT, USDC, Zcash, USD1, and Ripple USD (RLUSD).

The remaining 5% includes cryptocurrencies that are less liquid and harder to buy in large amounts.

#5275. Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 in 2026, More Than Triple 2025, Yet Without Binance the Year Ran Quieter: How Did Bitcoin and Ethereum React After Major Hacks?

Crypto hack losses hit $8.74B in 2026 vs $2.51B in 2025. Here’s how Bitcoin and Ether moved a day, a week and a month after major hacks.

Crypto hack losses reached $8.74 billion in 2026 by October 31, more than three times the $2.51 billion lost over the same ten months of 2025, after the October 29 Binance breach alone added $6.36 billion.

Take Binance out and the picture flips. The rest of 2026 comes to $2.38 billion, about 5% less than 2025 at the same point, even though attackers hit 325 targets against 120 a year earlier. More attacks, smaller hauls, and then one enormous one.

The market has its own pattern. Across the ten largest hacks since January 2025, Bitcoin’s move on the day of the attack ranged from -4.1% to +1.9%. A month later, for the nine with a full month of data, the range ran from -15.5% to +19.9%, and it followed whatever the broader market was doing.

The 2025 hacks landed in falling markets, and every one was followed by a lower Bitcoin price a month later. Most of 2026’s landed in rising ones.

So how bad has 2026 really been, and what does history say about the weeks after Binance?

The size of the biggest theft. Through September, 2026 was running behind 2025: $2.24 billion lost against $2.48 billion. Then Binance lost $6.36 billion across ten blockchains in one night, more than all of 2025’s hacks put together.

The two years share a culprit. The FBI tied 2025’s largest crypto hack, the $1.4 billion Bybit theft on February 21, to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Chainalysis now ties Binance to the same unit. The biggest hacks of each year:

The rest of 2026 looks different from 2025 too. There were 325 incidents through October, almost three times 2025’s 120, and five 2026 hacks topped $290 million, against one in 2025. Stolen keys and cross-chain bridges did most of the damage outside Binance.

The gross number also overstates what stays lost. CertiK’s October tally counts $3.03 billion frozen or returned, mostly Binance funds caught on-chain, which cuts the month’s adjusted losses to about $3.47 billion. Trackers also disagree on the year: CertiK puts 2026 at $9.2 billion gross and 2025 at $3.35 billion, while DefiLlama has $8.74 billion and $2.72 billion.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

A small dip on the day, then the market’s own trend. The heatmap compares Bitcoin and Ether with their close the day before each of the ten biggest hacks since 2025.

Bybit is the closest match to Binance: a North Korean exchange theft over $1 billion. Bitcoin lost 14.2% within a week of it, with US tariff fears weighing on markets that week too, and it was still 12.4% lower a month on.

Binance is following a gentler path so far. From the October 28 close to Monday:

Neither yet. Bitcoin trades at $77,870 on Binance, flat on the day, and has held above its October 30 low of $76,326 for three days, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average) at $76,512.

After Bybit, Bitcoin lost its floor within a week. After most of 2026’s hacks, it was higher a month later. The line between the two is clear on the chart: the 200-day EMA below, and the 50-day EMA at $80,293 above.

The crypto hack record says the first day rarely decides much. What Bitcoin does at the 200-day EMA over the next few weeks will show which path this one takes.

However, Bitcoin hasn’t outperformed traditional government bonds since then.

Per McGlone, the poor performance of the cryptocurrency may mean its best days are in the past.

#5273. THORChain founder rejects freeze request, CZ thanks Secret Service: Hodler’s Digest

Binance has reopened withdrawals following the world’s biggest ever hack, and THORChain co-founder argues it should not halt the protocol to comply with FBI demands.

Binance has reopened withdrawals for 15 blockchain networks, after $6.3 billion was stolen by North Korean hackers from its hot wallets late last week.

Binance said today it had processed around $4.65 billion in withdrawals after reopening and received $1 billion in deposits. Founder Changpeng Zhao said that in the first 12 hours there had only been a 2.1% net outflow and that “98% choose to stay!”

DeFi Llama’s Binance wallet tracker shows $5.8 billion in outflows over 24 hours, however its figures may include internal transfers or movements into new hot wallets.

About 95% of the stolen crypto has already been replenished, using a mixture of Binance’s corporate reserves, insurance and 50% of the funds in the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).

The biggest hack in history happened on Thursday, when North Korea’s TraderTraitor group gained access to delegated wallet permissions via a compromised laptop. Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph that attackers could have stolen the funds without using EIP-7702 (account abstraction), but it may have helped them bypass safeguards and drain assets in one sweep.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng rejected the idea the hack could be attributed to a single compromised laptop.

“To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action,” he said. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.”

Zhao thanked the Secret Service today for “acting within minutes to help track and freeze stolen funds... your speed, expertise and dedication helped contain the damage.”

Elliptic estimated that about $2.84 billion of the stolen assets, mostly USDC and USDT, had been frozen on chain leaving the hackers with $3.33 billion. The attacker raced against time to beat the unprecedented stablecoin blocks by borrowing about $44.6 million of ETH against stablecoins on Aave.

The FBI attributed blame for the attack to the TraderTraitor hackers, which is associated with North Korea’s Lazarus Group and were also blamed for multibillion hacks of Bybit and Bitget. President Donald Trump indicated “we’ll talk to North Korea about it.” The FBI also released a list of addresses connected to the hack and pointedly singled out THORnode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses.

The North Korean hackers have used THORChain to permissionlessly swap cryptocurrencies following previous attacks, and the price of the protocol’s native token RUNE jumped 13% in expectation of all those fees. Unfortunately for TraderTraitor, nine chains on THORChain, including Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tron, are currently halted after automated systems paused the protocol for unrelated reasons on October 31.

According to THORChain developer Chad Barraford on the Unchained podcast, only around 50 or so individuals operate the 100 THORChain nodes. If the node operators refuse to halt the protocol or block addresses, as seems likely based on past incidents and public statements, there is speculation they could face prosecution given the scale of the thefts and the involvement of the FBI and Secret Service.

THORChain founder JP Thor (who claims he is no longer involved) argued strongly that THORNode operators should not cooperate and should remain true to the ideals of decentralization and permissionlessness. “IMO if THORNodes decided to take the protocol offline next week then the experiment is over,” he said.

If one third plus one of THORnode operators vote in favor they can halt activity. Nodes can also leave the network if they do not wish to process the funds. THORChain can operate with as few as four nodes processing transactions.

Lookonchain reports the attackers have also been using cross chain platform Relay to swap about half of $95.9 million of stolen SOL into Bitcoin.

Crypto related stocks including Coinbase, Circle and Strategy sold off sharply following the hack, and crypto markets took a dive. But Strive CEO Matt Cole commented on Friday that Bitcoin had held up better than expected.

“I do have conviction that over any reasonable time frame, this does not change the investment thesis on Bitcoin,” Cole said. Bitcoin bottomed out around $76.5K and had recovered to 77,745 at the time of writing. In the wake of the attack, Nasdaq-listed firm Next Technology Holding announced its board has approved selling off its 5833 Bitcoin Treasury worth around $450 million.

The attackers have reportedly amassed at least 18,000 Bitcoin and 430,000 Ether from the theft and subsequent swaps, although some tallies of the funds in the addresses identified by the FBI put the tally much higher at 551,612 ETH and 18,270 BTC. There are concerns that if those currencies are sold off quickly, that it would put downward pressure on BTC and ETH prices.

Meanwhile, Senator Cynthia Lummis and The Digital Chamber both used the hack to again push for crypto legislation to help prevent and mitigate the effects of future attacks.

Trezor has urged customers who bought its hardware wallets from former authorized reseller CryptoBilis since March to move their funds after a report of a suspected implant in a Safe 5 device.

Trezor said Friday that a customer in Indonesia reported an unauthorized circuit board inside a Trezor Safe 5 bought on Tokopedia in August. Trezor said it had not yet examined the device and had received no reports of related losses.

The warning follows reports of crypto losses involving Ledger wallets sold through CryptoBilis that surfaced on Oct. 9. Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in one device.

At the end of the week, Bitcoin (BTC) is down 3% to trade at $77,745, Ethereum (ETH) is down 3.5% to trade at $2,260 and XRP (XRP) is down 3.9% to $1.02. The total market cap is at $2.21 trillion according to CoinMarketCap.

Among the biggest 100 cryptocurrencies, the top three altcoin winners of the week are Hyperliquid (HYPE) with a 13.7% gain, Midnight (NIGHT) on 12.6%, and Pepe (PEPE) on 12.6%.

The top three altcoin losers of the week are Curve DAO (CRV) which was down 18.6%, VeChain (VET) down 15.9% and Worldcoin down 13.8%.

Standard Chartered’s Geoffrey Kendrick said one big winner from the hack was likely to be decentralized exchanges and reaffirmed his conviction in Uniswap and the UNI token.

“The decentralized exchange [Uniswap] has never had any exploits, and the hack of the largest centralized exchange, in Binance, should see the ratio of DEX to CEX trading continue to increase.”The ratio is currently around 23.5%. Kendrick said he retains his $100 price target for Uniswap (UNI) for 2030. He said the Binance hack is “another reason why that forecast may end up being too low.”

CFTC chair Mike Selig says autonomous AI agents could challenge financial rules built around human traders, and regulators need to adapt. Selig said Super Intelligence (SI) could give smaller traders and businesses access to risk-management that was once reserved for larger institutions.

“SI can help process the vast amount of information significantly faster than human brain power and with greater accuracy,” he said.

But greater autonomy also comes with new risks. Agents could react unexpectedly to market conditions, while those using similar models could generate correlated trading behavior. The speed of autonomous transactions could also complicate market surveillance and risk management, he said.

Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis said it was targeted in a cybersecurity incident, similar to those suffered recently by other platforms.

“Based on the investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to investigation content, authentication credentials, or session tokens,” it said in a blog post on Friday. Some non-sensitive customer data was exposed, including user IDs, names and email addresses.

Chainalysis said it was using large language models to review its security and added the incident was not related to the recent crypto theft at Binance.

Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced to 180 months and 186 months in prison, respectively, for their armed robbery of cryptocurrency and kidnapping of a family in Grant, Minnesota.

The brothers were sentenced on Thursday before US District Judge Donovan W. Frank, according to a Friday news release. They had pleaded guilty in June.

On Sept. 19, 2025, the brothers, who had traveled from Texas to Minnesota, kidnapped Victim 1 and his family in their home at gunpoint, court documents said. They zip‑tied the family at gunpoint and held them for more than nine hours, demanding access to Victim 1’s cryptocurrency accounts.

In typical Bitcoin style, the number one cryptocurrency turns 18 amid AI-driven security threats, quantum fears and the biggest exchange hack in crypto history.

Attackers raced to convert stolen stablecoins into crypto that issuers could not freeze as industry players like Tether and Circle moved to immobilize billions of dollars in assets.

A US fusion startup says it has turned mercury into gold. Could a potential increase in the gold supply strengthen Bitcoin’s claim to be a better form of digital gold?

#5271. Do Not Use Your iPhone as Hardware Wallet, OneKey Founder

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Using an old iPhone as a crypto cold wallet may be less safe than it looks, OneKey founder Yishi Wang has warned. The practice is popular with self-custody fans: wipe a spare phone, take it offline, and keep your wallet recovery information on it.

Wang's worry is that an offline phone can still be attacked by someone who has it in their hands. He has pointed to flaws in several generations of iPhone. These include the publicly documented checkm8 issue on older models and, more recently reported, low-level weaknesses in certain later devices. They sit in the early stages of the boot process. A malicious app isn't involved.

An iOS update may not fix a weakness built into immutable boot code. Switching off Wi-Fi and cellular does nothing about someone who gets physical access to the phone. A vulnerability still doesn't automatically mean an attacker can recover a seed phrase, though. Device encryption, passcode strength and secure key handling remain real barriers.

Wang advises against trusting iPhone 11-generation and older devices with recovery phrases. If you think a phrase may have been exposed, create a completely new one using a trusted setup and move your funds to that wallet. Generating another address from the same seed won't help, because the underlying exposure stays.

He also stresses updated operating systems, long alphanumeric passcodes and careful control of USB connections. Earlier, he suggested that even newer iPhones shouldn't be treated as equivalent to purpose-built signing devices when the holdings are substantial and long-term.

Dedicated hardware wallets are built to isolate signing keys and let you check transaction details on the device itself. They carry risk too. Counterfeit hardware, compromised distribution channels and sloppy recovery-phrase handling can all undermine their security.

The argument is about threat models, not brand loyalty. An offline phone cuts remote exposure, but that doesn't turn it into a secure hardware wallet.

Ripple's scheduled November escrow unlock has put 1 billion XRP into circulation, with blockchain data tracker Whale Alert reporting two transactions in this regard.

🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 500,000,000 $XRP (626,430,089 USD) unlocked at #Ripple https://t.co/ejC9qFmsjb

Ripple's monthly unlocks are part of the firm's ongoing process to increase transparency and predictability around XRP distribution. The company initially put 55 billion XRP in escrow and released it in an organized fashion over time to manage the supply of XRP entering circulation.

But not all of the 1 billion XRP that was released stays on the market. In the past, Ripple has returned a large portion of the unlocked XRP (about 700 million XRP) to escrow while keeping some of it to facilitate operational needs, liquidity, and ecosystem-related activities.

The XRP Ledger is set for crucial fixes and improvements over the next few days. According to XRPScan data, fixCleanup3_4_0, which began its two-week activation window on Oct 21, 2026, after a reset in voting, now eyes the earliest activation date being 2:46 PM UTC on Nov 4, 2026.

Validator support for the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment must stay above 80% for it to activate. If it slips to 80% or lower even once, the amendment is rejected and the 14-day timer starts over.

This fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment is a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment is essential for Permission Delegation, which went live in October, as until it is enabled, users would not be able to delegate the PaymentBurn granular permission.

#5269. Horizen Holders Face November 4 Bridge Cutoff Before L3 Wind-Down

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Horizen users have a near-term operational deadline as the project winds down its layer-three network. Its official migration notice sets November 4 at 13:00 UTC as the bridge cutoff and directs holders to review the instructions for their particular assets.

The migration plan includes a later recovery process for certain remaining balances. That is not a universal guarantee for every token or wallet arrangement, making the difference between an ordinary withdrawal and a delayed recovery especially important.

A chain shutdown is different from a token being removed from an exchange. In the exchange case, the underlying network may continue to function normally. A network wind-down changes the infrastructure through which users can submit instructions and applications can update state.

That makes the location of an asset consequential. A token bearing the same name can exist in more than one environment, and the procedure for moving it depends on where the balance is actually recorded. A holder should not infer their position from a ticker in a portfolio tracker alone.

There is also a timing distinction between initiating an exit and receiving its result. Bridging can involve stages that finish after the first transaction. A successful submission is useful evidence, but the recipient-side balance and the bridge’s own status determine whether the transfer has completed.

Horizen says its later DAO return covers ZEN and qualifying ETH balances, while USDC.e is outside that process. The notice also flags special handling for smart-contract wallets and a minimum ETH balance threshold. Readers with affected holdings need the current official instructions rather than a generic assumption that all balances will be returned automatically.

These distinctions reflect an important feature of blockchain accounting: recognizing an address on two networks does not establish that the same kind of account exists on both. A simple wallet and a contract-controlled account can require different treatment when balances are reconstructed elsewhere.

Similarly, a bridged asset may be operated through infrastructure with obligations separate from those of the chain’s own project. A recovery programme can only make reliable promises about assets and processes within its stated scope.

The project attributes the accelerated transition to compatibility issues connected to Base’s Denim upgrade. Base’s published specification introduces a different block cadence and associated data changes, illustrating why infrastructure built on another chain must track its dependencies.

A layered system can borrow useful components and reduce development work. It can also inherit assumptions about how the underlying network behaves. When those assumptions change, the dependent service may need a migration rather than a routine version update.

This is a broader architectural lesson rather than evidence that all layer-three networks face the same outcome. The relevant question is which exact dependencies a system has and whether its operators can adapt them before an upstream change takes effect.

Moving activity to an established network can simplify the number of places where an ecosystem must maintain infrastructure. For users, however, the immediate benefit depends on successful balance transfers, working applications and clear communication about what happens to existing positions.

A staking interface being unavailable, for example, would not by itself establish that funds have disappeared. Equally, a roadmap promising future staking would not prove that a particular balance has already migrated. Transaction records and official recovery notices answer those different questions.

The November 4 cutoff is therefore the central fact for this week. The broader move to Base can be evaluated over time, but the asset-specific exit and recovery instructions deserve attention before the operating environment changes.

Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals after identifying a security incident in one of its systems on November 2. The Brazilian crypto exchange later published destination wallet addresses to help trace assets connected to the incident.

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company froze over 4.5 million USDT connected to the case. It is amongst other security incidents concerning crypto services, including Binance and old BTCPay Server software users, in the last few days.

Arkham separately valued wallets it attributed to the attacker at approximately $46 million on November 2. The tracked portfolio also included about $5.03 million in USDT, $3.02 million in USDC, $1.78 million in PEPE, $1.63 million in AAVE, and $1.46 million in PAX Gold.

Mercado Bitcoin responded quickly after discovering the breach; they claim it occurred overnight and that customers were financially unaffected while no data was lost.

They are investigating, tracking, and coordinating with the relevant authorities; deposits and withdrawals were stopped.

Following this, in a separate address, Mercado Bitcoin issued details of the addresses used on other blockchains for its transfers, including Bitcoin, Solana, Stellar, Tron, and their Ethereum-based/compatible services. It claimed the addresses were being published purely for tracing purposes.

The exchange also said it was working to restore operations safely and would keep customers informed through official channels. But there was no update about the reopening time or total financial impact.

Ardoino disclosed Tether’s intervention while sharing Mercado Bitcoin’s initial announcement.

“Tether froze more than 4.5M USDT related to this security incident,” he wrote.

Tether can block transfers of its tokens at specific addresses, helping restrict their movement during an investigation. This was the second time in the last seven days that Tether has frozen funds associated with exploits. The latest was with Binance, when over $6 billion was exploited.

Ardoino’s announcement left the next steps for those frozen tokens unspecified, including their possible return to Mercado Bitcoin.

The incident follows Binance’s disclosure that attackers stole approximately $6.3 billion from its wallets on October 29. Binance began reopening withdrawals on November 1 and committed to covering the losses.

BTCPay Server issued an advisory of their own on November 2 after receiving reports that Bitcoin and Litecoin were stolen from wallets that stored the spending keys on impacted servers.

They found web servers from version 2.4.1 or less were targeted, and the bad actors were also able to exploit a vulnerability that they patched in August through another method.

BTCPay recommends moving to fresh servers and moving existing wallet/seed to the new one, since updating the affected software might leave an open door for hackers.

The team added that wallets with their spending keys held outside the servers, like most hardware wallets, were unaffected by these thefts. It continues investigating the scope of the incident fully.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. A reported $1.1 billion in NEAR Protocol derivatives open interest has put the spotlight on speculative positioning in the token. The exact figure and its timing need confirmation at the exchange level. The general point holds either way: leveraged trading magnifies both optimism and downside when interest in an asset picks up.

Open interest is the notional value of futures and perpetual futures contracts that are still open. Daily trading volume is something else, a count of transactions over a period. Rising open interest means more positions are staying active. It doesn't say whether traders as a group expect prices to rise or fall, since every contract has exposure on both sides.

NEAR's derivatives participation has been swining before. In October open interest climbed above $1 billion and approached $1.9 billion during a strong price rally, then a pullback.

To read a fresh increase, analysts usually compare open interest with spot price, funding rates, trading volume and liquidation data. When price and open interest rise together, the market often reads that as growing risk appetite. If prices fall while open interest stays high, crowded leveraged positions become vulnerable to forced exits.

Funding rates are just another source of data. Sustained positive funding can suggest stronger demand for leveraged longs, and negative funding a preference for shorts. Neither is conclusive alone, and differences between exchanges can muddy comparisons.

NEAR's longer-term prospects depend on more than derivatives. Transaction costs, ecosystem integrations and adoption of cross-chain infrastructure such as NEAR Intents are more longer-term drivers. Speculative positioning can move the price fast, but it is no substitute for durable demand for blockchain services.

New leveraged positions must be backed by spot-market buying and healthy liquidity in order to have relevance. A large open-interest figure shows attention, nothing more. It isn't a forecast. Check it across data providers and manage risk carefully.

#5266. Devcon Opens in Mumbai This Week With Ethereum Builders Facing a Delivery Test

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

For people following Ethereum from the market side, the useful task is to separate ideas presented on a stage from changes that developers can actually test and users can eventually rely on. A conference creates a concentrated view of the work; it does not turn every proposal into a network commitment.

A protocol idea can be persuasive before its operational consequences are fully understood. It may improve one property, such as transaction handling, while adding costs elsewhere, such as data storage or the difficulty of running infrastructure.

The most informative technical presentations explain those trade-offs and offer a way for others to inspect the work. A specification, reproducible benchmark or test implementation gives outside developers something they can challenge. A performance target without those materials is harder to evaluate.

There is also a sequence between research, agreement on scope, client implementation, testing and activation. A talk about one stage should not be reported as completion of the next. This matters especially when short clips circulate without the qualifications that accompanied a presentation.

The Ethereum Foundation’s original Mumbai announcement described a gathering extending beyond protocol engineering. That wider participation matters because improvements in the underlying network only reach users through products, interfaces and operating processes.

A wallet team, for example, might need to turn a complex authorization into something a person can understand before signing. A payments developer needs to handle delayed confirmations and mistaken inputs. An institutional application needs to reconcile its blockchain records with the obligations in its legal agreements.

These are less dramatic achievements than a headline about speed, but they can determine whether an application is dependable. A credible demonstration should show what happens when the happy path breaks, including what a user sees and how the system recovers.

Open-source ecosystems distribute responsibility across people who do not all work for the same organization. A change can require cooperation among client teams, infrastructure operators, wallet developers and application maintainers, each with different constraints.

Bringing those groups together can shorten the distance between a proposed improvement and a clear understanding of its consequences. It can also expose disagreements that were easy to miss in a written thread. A resolved incompatibility may be a more useful outcome than another product announcement.

That kind of progress is difficult to measure through attendance figures. It becomes visible later, when documentation improves, implementations converge or a previously blocked integration starts working. The follow-up work is where a conference’s technical value is ultimately demonstrated.

Useful evidence will include published materials, specific engineering milestones and clearly identified owners for the next stage of a project. Readers should be able to distinguish a proposal seeking discussion from software ready for production.

For applications, the stronger indicators are working integrations and repeated use, alongside a credible explanation of costs and failure handling. A polished demonstration can establish that an idea is possible without proving that it works reliably at scale.

Devcon’s immediate importance is bringing Ethereum’s many development efforts into view at the same time. The longer-term story will depend on what survives scrutiny and becomes usable software. Neither the schedule nor a keynote provides a dependable forecast for ETH’s price.
